2. The respondent as petitioner filed this revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure challenging the legality and propriety of the judgment and order dated 17-5-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 3rd Court, Noakhali, in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 25 of 2005 allowing the appeal and thereby allowing pre-emption case by reversing the judgment and order dated 26-4-2005 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Begumgonj, Noakhali, in Miscellaneous case No. 113 of 2002 rejecting the Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case ex-parte which was filed under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. 

 3. The petitioner's case in short is that the opposite party No. 1 as pre-emptor instituted Miscellaneous Case No. 113 of 2002 before the Senior Assistant Judge, Begumgonj, Noakhali under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950, impleading 13 persons as pre-emptees, including the present petitioner No. 1 as pre-emptee opposite party No. 4 and her husband, the predecessor of the present petitioner No.2-6, as pre-emptee opposite party No. 3, stating interalia that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the related Jama by inheritance and also by purchase but without serving any notice of transfer upon him the case land was transferred vide kabala No. 2455 and 2462 dated 13-03-2000. He came to learn about the same on 08-11-2002 and then after obtaining the certified copy of the aforesaid kabala on 12-11-2002 filed the aforesaid miscellaneous case for pre-emption on 17-11-2002. 

 12. On the other hand the appellate court, being the final court of fact, found that the P.W.-1, the pre-emptor proved that on 8.11.2002, when the pre-emptee and his men entered into the case land and claimed to have purchased the same and thereafter when the pre-emptor got the certified copy of the registered kabala on 12.11.2002 and came to know about the sale and as such within 5(five) days he filed the pre-emption case on 17.11.2002 which is very much within the period of 4(four) months from the date of knowledge as provided under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act-1950. The appellate court also held that since the case has been disposed of ex-parte and since the date of knowledge of transfer was not challenged or denied by any body, the question of leading corroborative evidence in this regard does not necessarily arise. With such observation, the lower appellate court allowed the said miscellaneous appeal. 

 15. Thus considering the facts and circumstances stated above and the above noted decision I am of the opinion that the learned judge of the court of appeal committed error in law in passing the impugned judgment without considering the submissions of the respondents whom he heard earlier on 7-5-2007, and as such I am inclined to send down the case, on remand, to the appellate court for hearing the appeal afresh upon taking into consideration the submissions of both the parties, in accordance with law, in order to decide the material issue concerned in the case for ends of justice, and to dispose of the appeal in accordance with law, specifically taking into consideration Order XLI, rule 30 of the Code of Civil Procedure while delivering the judgment.
